title: Summer and Bakery
premise: August Ashgrove, a pastry chef whose beloved café is three missed payments from foreclosure, has spent fifteen years hiding from the scandal that ended her engagement and her career in London. When a snowstorm strands her overnight with Theo Marchetti—the rival pâtissier who was once her closest friend, fiercest competitor, and the man she abandoned on the worst night of their twenties—old grief and older love resurface. As Theo quietly buys her café's debt to save it, August must decide whether accepting help means surrendering the independence she built from ashes. In the end, they forgive themselves first, then each other, and reopen the bakery together as partners in flour and in life.
about_author: Xanthe Kavanagh is a former line cook turned novelist who writes love stories set in kitchens, believing that sugar, like forgiveness, works best under pressure. She lives in a coastal town where she tests every recipe that appears in her books.

chapters.title: Three Payments Left
chapters.summary: August's POV. Opening on a gray Tuesday, August counts the café's dwindling accounts while perfecting a cardamom bun recipe her late grandmother taught her. A foreclosure notice arrives. The beat: quiet dread masked by competence, establishing what she stands to lose.

chapters.title: The Man on the Menu
chapters.summary: August's POV. A food magazine names Theo Marchetti 'Pâtissier of the Year'—with a photo of him holding a dessert August invented at twenty-three. Her hands shake frosting a cake. The beat: old betrayal reopened, showing the wound beneath her calm.

chapters.title: Flour Fight, Fifteen Years Ago
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Flashback chapter: young August and Theo as rival apprentices, trading sabotage and stolen kisses in a shared kitchen, culminating in the night everything broke—a competition, a confession, and August vanishing by morning. The beat: tender, reckless youth.

chapters.title: The Storm Warning
chapters.summary: August's POV. A regional baking expo forces August out of her safe radius; her supplier insists she attend or lose her contract. Forecast says blizzard. The beat: reluctant step outside comfort, duty versus fear.

chapters.title: Stranded
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The expo collapses early; roads close; August and Theo end up the last two guests snowed into a mountain inn with one working fireplace and a kitchen neither can resist inspecting. The beat: forced proximity, prickly banter masking panic.

chapters.title: What the Kitchen Remembers
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Unable to sleep, Theo finds August baking at 3 a.m.—muscle memory from their apprenticeship. They cook side by side without speaking, bodies remembering what minds refuse to. The beat: intimacy rekindled through craft, not words.

chapters.title: The Night We Don't Talk About
chapters.summary: August's POV. Trapped by the storm, they finally speak of the competition fifteen years ago—and August admits she didn't lose fairly; she froze, fled, and let Theo take the blame publicly. The beat: first confession, raw and incomplete.

chapters.title: Snowbound Sunday
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. One golden day before the roads open: they walk the frozen village, share stories of the lost years, and nearly kiss before Theo's phone rings with business he can't ignore. The beat: hope kindled, then interrupted.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: August's POV. Roads clear; both retreat into politeness. Back home, August throws herself into saving the café and discovers the bank has sold her loan—to an anonymous buyer. The beat: whiplash from warmth back to threat.

chapters.title: The Anonymous Creditor
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Revealed: Theo bought the debt intending to forgive it, but his lawyer warns that forgiving a competitor's loan could trigger an ethics review threatening his own empire. He must choose between reputation and August. The beat: love against duty, Theo's side.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: August's POV. The bank offers new terms: keep the café if she enters the same national competition that ruined her, judged by Theo himself. It smells like charity—or a trap. Pride wars with desperation. The beat: humiliation sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Notebook
chapters.summary: August's POV. Searching for a signature dish, August inherits more than recipes when she opens her grandmother's notebook and finds letters revealing her grandmother also chose safety over a great love. The beat: inheritance theme deepens; generational echo.

chapters.title: Practice Makes Wreckage
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo secretly drives four hours each week to watch August practice through the café window, coaching via anonymous notes left with flour deliveries. She starts to suspect. The beat: longing expressed sideways, guilt compounding.

chapters.title: Caught Red-Handed
chapters.summary: August's POV. August catches Theo leaving a note; fury erupts—she'd rather fail than be pitied or managed. He confesses he owns her debt. The beat: midpoint explosion; trust shattered just as it rebuilt.

chapters.title: The Ethics Hearing
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo's board demands he recuse or divest; his mentor offers him partnership abroad if he walks away clean. Theo realizes his gilded life was another form of hiding. The beat: Theo's mirror moment—he must forgive himself too.

chapters.title: Baking Alone
chapters.summary: August's POV. Lowest point: the café fails a health inspection triggered by an anonymous complaint, and August nearly signs the surrender papers. Her grandmother's letters pull her back—one line: 'Duty kept me small; don't let it shrink you.' The beat: dark night of the soul.

chapters.title: The Competition Begins
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. August competes; Theo, having resigned rather than recuse silently, sits in the audience as a spectator—not a judge. Rival chefs whisper about the scandal of fifteen years ago. The beat: rising tension, public stakes, private courage.

chapters.title: Cardamom and Confession
chapters.summary: August's POV. For the final round, August presents the dessert she abandoned at twenty-three, telling the judges—and the room—the truth about that night and the years of hiding. The beat: climax of self-forgiveness; reclaiming her name.

chapters.title: What Theo Did Next
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Before results are announced, Theo takes the stage, publicly clears August's name from the old scandal and announces he's dissolving his company's claim on her café. The beat: grand gesture earned, not cheap—sacrifice made real.

chapters.title: Second Place, First Choice
chapters.summary: August's POV. August wins second place—but a celebrated chef offers her a dream job abroad, the life she once wanted. She chooses the café, the town, and finally says yes to Theo, on equal footing. The beat: resolution of love against duty; choosing, not settling.

chapters.title: Reopening Day
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Spring: the café reopens with a new sign—Ashgrove & Marchetti. Old customers return; the health inspector brings flowers. Small safe steps, now taken together. The beat: warm payoff of every thread.

chapters.title: Summer, Finally
chapters.summary: August's POV, epilogue tone. One year later, August teaches a free baking class for kids who remind her of two young rivals, while Theo closes early to dance with her in the kitchen. The notebook gets a new entry in her handwriting. The beat: peace earned; memory transformed into inheritance.
